themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 6 reports THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 4700% increase (z-score: 17.76)—suggesting a sudden, coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Central Harlem.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (4700% spike)
Z-score of 17.76 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No prior spike of this magnitude in 90-day complaint dataset
reporting_angles: Interview 311 operators and Sanitation Department to determine if this reflects actual uptick or enforcement shift
Walk neighborhoods to document what kinds of postings (political, commercial, graffiti tags) are appearing and whether they're concentrated in specific blocks

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 5 reports THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1900% spike (z-score: 7.18)—indicating either aggressive new enforcement action or sudden vendor proliferation in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% spike)
Z-score of 7.18 indicates statistically significant departure
Convergence with CB budget requests for MWBE support suggests vendor community sensitivity
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and Dept. of Consumer Affairs to understand if new enforcement sweep began this week
Interview street vendors and community merchants about enforcement pressure; explore whether this affects immigrant-owned small businesses

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints increased to 4 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 256% spike (z-score: 3.68)—potentially signaling customer confusion over new conservation mandates or infrastructure disruptions.
evidence: 4 water conservation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (256% spike)
Z-score of 3.68 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Complements ongoing heat/hot water complaint volume (7,444 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Check DEP website and local news for any new water conservation notices or main breaks in Central Harlem
Contact residents filing complaints to understand whether they're responding to a city alert or experiencing service disruptions

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Resurgence
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 8 reports LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 1180% increase (z-score: 8.61)—signaling either a sudden tagging campaign or lag in removal services in Central Harlem.
evidence: 8 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1180% spike)
Z-score of 8.61 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Potential correlation with illegal posting spike THIS WEEK suggests broader disorder signal
reporting_angles: Document graffiti locations and tags to identify whether one crew is responsible or if it's endemic
Investigate Dept. of Sanitation removal capacity and response time in Central Harlem vs. other districts

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints increased to 46 reports LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 8.1 per week—a 466% spike (z-score: 4.08)—suggesting potential pothole, pavement, or traffic infrastructure failures concentrated in one area.
evidence: 46 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (466% spike)
Z-score of 4.08 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Related to broader infrastructure theme reflected in repeated CB capital budget requests for DOE and DEP
reporting_angles: Map the 46 complaints to identify if damage is concentrated on specific avenues or blocks
Interview DOT about any recent utility work, flooding, or weather damage that triggered deterioration
